manifestComparison.method: Compared complete old file/directory lists, bytes, SHA256, attributes and UTC times at 100ns precision. Compared the complete new 86-file bytes/hash list to the frozen candidate manifest. No old-library rehash was performed by this reviewer.

findings.text: Backup/deployment and approved offline-settings/cold-start evidence pass their limited checks. Two launches were counted and both exited normally; this does not establish UI-settings-click success or independent zero requests.

One original Start Menu shortcut changed to the new executable without its isolated profile argument. Its changed bytes were preserved and its original bytes/metadata/binding restored. Other current original-file inventories match baseline; isolation acceptance still fails.

The notification binding is directly observed. Frozen app and official Electron source support the proposed trigger chain, but no runtime trace proves the exact writer/timing and no historical registry baseline exists.
Renamed ambiguous zero-call exclusions to intentional task operations and qualified the overall failure cause. Explicitly distinguished current shortcut restoration from never having changed.

Original-shortcut and retained-app notification identities match. The single Registry64 default-value proposal may be submitted to the user, with bounded before/after metadata and ACL comparison; it has not been executed or authorized by this audit.

publicationScope: Only the sanitized result and this audit. No user data, machine identifiers, private paths, raw inventories or binaries are included. Candidate remains unapproved for use and not released.
